Subject: Control plane identity: mapping & provisioning approach for private deployment

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Falcon Health is proceeding with the private control plane deployment in our AWS VPC and we need to lock down identity/provisioning flows before the pilot starts. A few asks from our side: 

- Confirm whether Redwood supports SCIM 2.0 group-to-role provisioning (we need groups to map to RBAC roles in the control plane).
- How do you recommend mapping Okta attributes to Redwood IAM roles (we have custom attribute app_role and department).
- We also need guidance on SAML assertion mapping for SP-initiated logins to the private control plane UI (NameID vs email).

I'll attach our SAML metadata and our internal provisioning matrix. Can we schedule a short tech review with your infra team this week?

Thanks,
Jordan Ellis

Falcon Health

Subject: Re: Control plane identity: mapping & provisioning approach for private deployment

Team — looping you in to confirm the approach and owners. Jordan sent over Falcon's SAML metadata and a provisioning spreadsheet (attached). High-level constraints from the customer: 

- They require group-based provisioning into the control plane (SCIM -> groups -> RBAC).
- They use Okta as IdP; want SP-initiated SSO for admins and SAML for console access.
- Auditability: they want every control plane admin action tied to an Okta user identity; no shared service accounts if possible.

Proposed next steps for the review call: 
1) We validate SCIM mapping template from our side and propose a role matrix (I can draft).
2) Confirm SAML attribute mapping (NameID policy + app_role usage).
3) Outline IAM role assumptions for any AWS-side cross-account access (if we recommend an automated jump role).
4) Share our control plane IAM guidelines doc and a minimal checklist for on-prem network ACLs that affect SAML/SCIM endpoints.

Please see attached: redwood-scim-template.csv and rdw-controlplane-iam-guidelines.pdf. Mateo — can you confirm whether our SCIM service accepts group.membership as the authoritative source (vs group attribute mapping)? Vivek — can you prep the recommended AWS IAM role pattern if they want to integrate with a customer-managed KMS/HSM? Marissa — could you draft a simple role -> SCIM group matrix we can send to Jordan before the call?

Jordan — can you share preferred time slots? We can do a 45-minute technical sync and come with an implementation checklist.

—Kimberly Park

Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control plane identity: mapping & provisioning approach for private deployment

Kimberly / team / Jordan — draft role matrix attached and a few clarifications from an ops perspective: 

- SCIM behavior: our SCIM endpoint supports group membership sync where a SCIM Group maps to a Redwood RBAC role (create/update/delete). We can accept Okta's group push but recommend pushing groups scoped to the application (app-specific groups) to avoid noise.

- Recommended attribute mappings (Okta -> Redwood):
  • Okta.app_role -> rdw_role (string)
  • Okta.user.email -> email (primary identifier)
  • Okta.department -> department (used for read-only tags, not for privileges)

- SAML: we recommend NameID=email for consistency with audit logs. If customer insists on persistent NameID, we need a stable immutable attribute and to map that to the Control Plane's user_id field.

- AWS IAM note: If Falcon wants cross-account actions (e.g., for a private connector into their KMS), we'll propose a short-lived role-arn exchange with STS AssumeRole with session tags containing the Redwood user email. Vivek, I've put comments for you in the matrix about session tag requirements.

I've attached scim-role-matrix.csv (simple 4-role breakdown: superadmin, admin, operator, viewer) and an example Okta mapping snippet. Jordan — if you can confirm app_role values you use, we'll finalize. Also flagged a couple of edge cases: contractors (external identities) and service accounts — we recommend service accounts be managed as scoped app clients with restricted tokens rather than regular users.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Kimberly / Marissa / team — thanks, this is great and aligns with our internal requirements. Quick confirmations: 

- We use app_role values: SuperAdmin, OrgAdmin, DevOps, ReadOnly. We'll push Okta groups scoped to the app (Falcon-ControlPlane-*) to your SCIM endpoint.
- We are happy to use NameID=email. Our security team will accept email as the primary binding for auditability.
- For contractors, we will create separate external groups and mark them with an attribute contractor=true.

Next steps: 
1) I'm attaching our SAML metadata (falcon-saml-metadata.xml) and a link to the DocuSign envelope for a standard data-connector addendum: https://docusign.com/r/abc123-falcon-integration.
2) Okta Admin (cc'ed) will start a test integration against your staging SCIM/SAML endpoints once we get staging URLs and a short runbook.

Can Redwood provide a staging SP entity ID and ACS URL for the private control plane, plus a staging SCIM endpoint and a one-page runbook (curl examples and expected responses)? If you can push that by EOD Monday, we'll try a provisioning test on Tuesday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Jordan
Jordan Ellis

Falcon Health
